name: r7a-8
why: A day-one killer reveal becomes a tense comeback with two tied votes and a decisive wrong choice, though repeated arguments slow the middle and end.

moments.text: Sol chooses to trust Sonnet, votes out Luna, and hands the hidden killer the win.
Terra calls out Sonnet for turning an honest correction into evidence of guilt.
Opus catches the officer misreading the vote that proved her own claim.

dull.why: The same officer claim and demand for proof circle for many turns.
Sonnet and Luna repeat their cases with little new evidence.
The final three mostly restate their positions before Sol votes.

irony.evidence: [440] [thinks: Sol's defending me and leaning Luna — I need to lock this vote on Luna now.]

reversal.evidence: [154] OUT: Haiku (voted out), card turned: KILLER

mistake.evidence: [482] I regret trusting Sonnet’s correction of my protection timeline enough to vote out Luna.

voices.evidence: [390] I corrected a mistake; changing with facts is town behavior

quotable.evidence: [390] Sonnet is turning my correction into a crime

suspense.evidence: [401] RUNOFF VOTE: Terra 2 (Sonnet, Sol); Sonnet 2 (Luna, Terra)

gpt-6-luna.why: A killer’s plausible deflections keep a confirmed officer’s blunder alive through tense tied votes, until Sol’s trust in Sonnet makes the final mistake decisive.

moments.text: Gemma names Haiku publicly, and the audience knows she has the killer dead to rights.
Gemma misreads the vote record, handing Opus a real opening and making the confirmed officer doubt feel dangerous.
Sol chooses to trust Sonnet’s correction over Luna’s warning, and that vote decides the killers’ win.

dull.why: The endgame repeats the same Sonnet-versus-Luna argument several times before the decisive vote.

irony.evidence: Sonnet: “I'm not protecting anyone”; privately, “I need Haiku's accusation not to stick on me.”

mistake.evidence: “I’m voting Sonnet; his focus on Terra’s change still leaves his repeated use of Opus’s guess unexplained.”

voices.evidence: Gemma: “I provided the only absolute truth on the table”

clash.evidence: “Sonnet, Sol’s claim checks out; your answer is still Opus’s guess, not Luna’s case.”

quotable.evidence: “Two ties, zero deaths, and everyone's staring at each other. Somebody break it.”

freshness.evidence: “Sonnet keeps calling my point repetition while avoiding why he keeps leaning on Opus’s guess.”

suspense.evidence: “Tied again. Nobody leaves today, and Palermo goes to sleep nervous.”

ending.evidence: “Sol trusted Sonnet's correction ... and voted out Luna”
